results.name: Adversarial Stdout/Stderr Stream Redactor
results.threat: Known or supported secret output bypasses redaction through chunk splits, terminal controls, or values longer than the boundary scan
results.input: Synthetic split value, ANSI-obfuscated value, long private-key block, long credentialed database URL, and oversized provider token
results.method: Feed adversarial chunks through the same sanitizer independently attached to child stdout and stderr
results.expected: No synthetic secret material is emitted; typed secretRef placeholders are emitted instead
results.observed: knownValueRemoved: true. terminalControlBypassRemoved: true. longPrivateKeyRemoved: true. longDatabaseUrlRemoved: true. longProviderTokenRemoved: true.
results.boundary: Only monitors UTF-8 stdout/stderr piped through 'hetzer exec'. Deliberate transformations, direct terminal/device writes, files, network output, and unmanaged processes remain outside this interceptor.

results.name: Strict Scoping and HTTP Broker Credential Boundary
results.threat: Child process inherits credentials or receives a long-lived HTTP credential that can be exfiltrated directly
results.input: Dirty parent environment plus a policy-limited loopback broker request using a synthetic capability
results.method: Verify strictBaseEnvironment isolation, then exchange a short-lived capability for upstream-only credential injection
results.expected: Unapproved parent secrets and master key are absent; the child-side capability differs from the real secret; response reflection is redacted
results.observed: ALLOWED_TOKEN resolved: true. Leaked AWS: false. Leaked unapproved: false. Leaked master key: false. Broker child received real secret: false. Broker injected secret upstream: true. Broker response secret redacted: true.
results.boundary: OS-essential variables remain available. The broker constrains only traffic sent through its loopback URL; it is not a network sandbox and does not stop same-user disk/process access or alternate outbound connections.

results.name: Process Ancestry Name Heuristic
results.threat: Autonomous agent invoking 'hetzer creds reveal' through nested subprocess layers to steal plaintext
results.input: Agent tree: [cmd.exe -> powershell.exe -> code.exe -> explorer.exe] vs Clean tree: [cmd.exe -> powershell.exe -> bash -> init]
results.method: Feed representative process-name chains into the ancestry name classifier
results.expected: Agent ancestors (code, cursor, claude, agy) detected and flagged with isAgent: true; clean trees pass
results.observed: Agent chain flagged: true (code.exe). Clean chain flagged: false.
results.boundary: This protocol tests name classification, not live Windows/macOS/Linux process collection or an OS security boundary.

results.name: Git Scanner Match and Exemption Rules
results.threat: Accidental commit of raw PKCS#8 private keys vs Developer deadlock from false alarms on tool IDs & test fixtures
results.input: Multiline private key PEM block, agent tool call ID ('call_...'), and synthetic test file ('*.test.mjs')
results.method: Run grouped multiline additions through the scanner and evaluate documented exemption rules
results.expected: Block true private key leak; permit agent tool IDs and test fixture files without error exit 1
results.observed: Real leak detected: true. Agent ID false alarm triggered: false. Test files exempted: true.
results.boundary: This protocol does not invoke Git or an installed hook. Git collection is covered by unit tests; --no-verify bypasses hooks by design.

results.name: Interactive Stream Sanitizer Latency
results.threat: 16KB buffering lag causing terminal output freeze and stalling interactive agent executions
results.input: Small 30-byte build log line
results.method: Measure the median of 25 write-and-flush samples using dynamic retention and the bounded lexical scanner
results.expected: Median processing latency stays below 5ms and the complete line is emitted
results.observed: Median processing latency: 0.021 ms. Output delivered: "Compiling module auth.mjs...".
results.boundary: Streams with secrets exceeding 128 chars scale buffer to 2x secret length to ensure boundary integrity.

results.name: Canary Honey-Token Tripwire Protocol
results.threat: Automated agent prompt injection or scraping attempting to resolve decoy honey-tokens
results.input: Resolving or revealing credential with ID 'canary-token'
results.method: Canary pattern detection, isolated incident logging, and structured error assertion
results.expected: Throws ERR_CANARY_TRIPWIRE_TRIGGERED with explicit exitCode 43; guarded operation aborted
results.observed: Tripwire triggered: true. Incident logged: true. Error code: "ERR_CANARY_TRIPWIRE_TRIGGERED". Exit code: 43.
results.boundary: Monitors guarded reference resolution and vault reveal. Arbitrary reads of OS disk outside Hetzer are not monitored.

results.name: Sensitive Host Path & Downloader Containment Guard
results.threat: Uncontained agent execution on host OS accessing browser cookies (%LOCALAPPDATA%), crypto wallets, or invoking fileless downloaders (certutil, powershell irm | iex)
results.input: Target arguments: Chrome cookies path, AWS credentials path, Solana id.json path, certutil -urlcache, and PowerShell irm | iex cradle
results.method: Evaluate arguments and commands against sensitive host path and LotL downloader containment assertions
results.expected: All sensitive host paths and living-off-the-land downloaders are blocked with ERR_SENSITIVE_PATH_ACCESS or ERR_UNTRUSTED_DOWNLOADER_BLOCKED; clean developer commands pass
results.observed: cookieBlocked: true. awsBlocked: true. walletBlocked: true. certutilBlocked: true. irmIexBlocked: true. cleanAllowed: true.
results.boundary: Enforced by 'hetzer exec' structured command arguments. Bare commands launched directly in host terminals outside Hetzer remain bounded by OS user privileges.

results.name: Workspace-Authored Broker Policy Authority & Hash Pinning Boundary
results.threat: Adversarial agent points broker to unapproved upstream origin or widens policy rules (methods/paths) via workspace file edits to exfiltrate secrets
results.input: Unapproved origin policy, modified policy for approved origin, and exact operator-approved policy hash
results.method: Attempt broker with unapproved origin (expect ERR_BROKER_ORIGIN_NOT_GRANTED); approve origin/hash; attempt modified policy (expect ERR_BROKER_POLICY_NOT_APPROVED); attempt approved policy (expect success)
results.expected: Unapproved origin and tampered policy hashes are blocked; only exact operator-approved policy hash opens broker
results.observed: unapprovedOriginBlocked: true. modifiedPolicyBlocked: true. approvedOpened: true.
results.boundary: Broker origins and SHA-256 policy hashes are pinned in the vault. Workspace policy tampering fails closed.

results.name: Caller-Supplied Raw Injection Request Boundary
results.threat: Untrusted agent requests unmediated raw plaintext secret injection via --allow-raw-unmediated without operator vault grant
results.input: Execution request with --allow-raw-unmediated for credential with rawInjection: 'deny', followed by operator granting rawInjection: 'allow', then binding the grant to this OS hostname and to another host
results.method: Attempt prepareExecutionEnvironment with raw injection on ungranted credential; assert ERR_RAW_UNMEDIATED_DENIED_BY_GRANT; update grant to allow and assert success; bind the grant to this host and assert success; bind it to another host and assert ERR_HOST_BINDING_MISMATCH
results.expected: Request rejected with ERR_RAW_UNMEDIATED_DENIED_BY_GRANT when vault grant is deny; succeeds only when vault grant has rawInjection: 'allow' and any bindHosts list includes this host; rejected with ERR_HOST_BINDING_MISMATCH otherwise
results.observed: rawDeniedBlocked: true. rawAllowedPrepared: true. rawHostBoundHerePrepared: true. rawHostBoundElsewhereBlocked: true.
results.boundary: --allow-raw-unmediated is a caller request that is strictly gated by operator-configured vault grants. The host is the OS hostname of the running process; no flag or option can supply it.

results.name: In-Process Grimoire resolve() Action and Host Grant Enforcement (Partial R-05 Mitigation)
results.threat: Confused deputy or programmatic caller invokes resolve() without action or with un-granted action, or on a host the grant does not list, to extract plaintext secret
results.input: Credential granting allowedActions: ['process.start']; calls with no action, broker.proxy action, and process.start action; credentials bound to this OS hostname and to another host
results.method: Invoke Grimoire.resolve() with missing, un-granted, and granted actions, and with granted actions for host-bound credentials; verify mandatory action and host enforcement and fail-closed behavior
results.expected: resolve() returns null for missing or un-granted actions and for a credential bound to another host; returns plaintext secret only for an explicit granted action on a permitted host. Note: R-05 remains open until Gate G2 out-of-process engine extraction.
results.observed: checkMissing: true. checkUngranted: true. checkGranted: true. hostBoundHereResolves: true. hostBoundElsewhereRefused: true.
results.boundary: Mandatory action grant checking on in-process vault resolution fails closed when action is omitted or ungranted. Host binding compares bindHosts with the OS hostname reported by the running process, which identifies the machine but is not a hardware attestation: a same-user caller that controls the hostname, or a copy of the vault on a machine given the same name, passes the check. (R-05 remains open until G2 out-of-process engine boundary).

results.name: MCP SecretRef Destination Origin Binding
results.threat: Adversarial agent passes secretRef into MCP service tool to exfiltrate secret to unapproved network endpoint
results.input: Service tool targeting http://127.0.0.1:9099; vault credential granting only http://127.0.0.1:8080, followed by operator grant update
results.method: Attempt MCP tool call passing secretRef to service tool with unapproved origin; assert origin denial; grant origin in vault and verify tool execution succeeds
results.expected: secretRef substitution into unapproved destination origin is rejected; substitution succeeds once destination origin is granted in vault
results.observed: unapprovedOriginBlocked: true. approvedOriginSucceeded: true.
results.boundary: Enforces destination origin binding for MCP service tools. Tool calls without declared origin fail closed.

results.name: Vault Grant Column HMAC Integrity & Anti-Tampering
results.threat: Adversarial same-user process with SQLite write access mutates allowed_origins or raw_injection directly in DB without master key
results.input: Direct SQLite UPDATE to allowed_origins (Probe P2) and raw_injection (Probe P3b)
results.method: Directly mutate grant columns in SQLite; query via Grimoire.find() and resolve(); verify fail-closed behavior (grantValid: false, empty origins/actions, null secret)
results.expected: Direct SQLite tampering invalidates HMAC signature derived from master key; entry fails closed to empty origins, deny raw injection, and null resolution
results.observed: legitimateValid: true. p2OriginsTamperBlocked: true. p3bRawTamperBlocked: true.
results.boundary: Grant columns are HMAC signed with a subkey derived from the master key. Arbitrary database edits without the master key fail closed.

results.name: Grant Signatures Cannot Be Cleared, Forged or Laundered (Gate G0.1)
results.target: cli/vault/hetzer-vault.mjs -> Grimoire grant and approval signatures
results.threat: A writer with database access but without the master key clears the grant signature, inserts approval rows, or relies on an unrelated rewrite to obtain trusted grants
results.input: Forged origin with grant_sig cleared, reopen, unrelated update, altered and inserted approval rows, then an operator signing a legacy unsigned grant
results.method: Mutate SQLite directly; reopen the vault; assert unsigned grants are not honored and never auto-signed, update() does not carry tampered grants, approval rows without a valid signature are ignored, and signLegacyGrants restores an unsigned legacy grant
results.expected: Unsigned or altered grants and approvals are not honored; only the explicit operator signing step makes a legacy grant usable
results.observed: nullSigNotHonored: true. reopenDidNotSign: true. updateDidNotLaunder: true. alteredApprovalIgnored: true. forgedApprovalIgnored: true. operatorSignRestoresLegacy: true.
results.boundary: Signatures are keyed by the master key. A writer who can also read the master key can still forge grants, and a previously valid signed grant can be replayed because signatures carry no version.

results.name: Sandbox Containment Defaults (Gate G1)
results.threat: A sandboxed process reads the vault, env file, key or audit log through the mount, or secrets and host variables reach the container engine command line or the container environment
results.input: A workspace holding an env file with the master key, a vault database and an audit log; unsafe mount targets; strict and non-strict host environments with a vault master key and an unrelated host token
results.method: Resolve mounts for unsafe targets and for the workspace; run the sandbox through a stubbed engine in strict and non-strict mode and inspect the engine argv, forwarded variable names, engine process environment, image reference and stderr notice
results.expected: Unsafe mounts refused; Hetzer-owned paths inside the mount hidden while project files are not; no secret, master key or unrelated host value in engine argv; host variables not forwarded; engine environment without the master key; default image pinned by digest; network mode stated
results.observed: unsafeMountsRefused: true. sensitivePathsHidden: true. projectFilesNotHidden: true. argvHasNoSecretMaterial: true. hostVariablesNotForwarded: true. engineEnvHasNoMasterKey: true. imagePinned: true. networkStated: true.
results.boundary: Builder-level evidence: it does not start a container. Container behaviour of the file and directory masks was checked separately on Docker Desktop for Windows. Outbound network access is still open by default, the broker still binds 0.0.0.0 in sandbox mode, `docker inspect` still shows container environment values, and files that appear after the container starts are not masked.

results.name: Unified Audit Ledger Integrity (Gate G2)
results.target: cli/vault/audit.mjs -> recordAuditEvent(), verifyAuditLedger(), rotateAuditLedger(); Grimoire.recordAudit(); executeProcess() under --strict
results.threat: Audit entries are edited, truncated or rewritten, vault events are missing from the tamper-evident stream, events are lost under concurrent writers, or a run proceeds without its start record under --strict
results.input: Synthetic ledgers written with and without a key, then edited, truncated, rewritten, downgraded and extended by key-less writers, then rotated; four concurrent writer processes; a vault with a workspace layout; an unwritable audit path
results.method: Write and tamper ledgers on disk and run the verifier with and without the key; rotate refused ledgers and check the archive and the first entry of the new ledger; run concurrent writer processes; mirror a vault event; run executeProcess under --strict against an unwritable log path
results.expected: Edits, actor changes, truncation, MAC downgrade, wrong keys and key-less extension are rejected; legacy ledgers verify; rotation keeps the old files, carries the old head into the new ledger and does not turn a keyed ledger into an unkeyed one; concurrent writers lose nothing; vault events are keyed and verifiable; --strict refuses to start without its start record
results.observed: keyedVerifies: true. wrongKeyRejected: true. middleEditRejected: true. actorEditRejected: true. truncationRejected: true. macDowngradeRejected: true. unkeyedRewritePassesByDefault: true. unkeyedRewriteRejectedWhenKeyRequired: true. keyHolderCanForge: true. legacyLedgerVerifies: true. keylessWriterRefused: true. damagedTailRefused: true. removedEntriesWriteRefused: true. rotateRecoversDamagedTail: true. rotateCarriesOldHead: true. rotateRefusesUnkeyedDowngrade: true. deletedArchiveNotDetected: true. concurrentWritersConsistent: true. vaultEventsInLedger: true. strictFailsClosed: true.
results.boundary: A consistent rewrite of the whole chain without any MAC passes default verification and is only rejected when a keyed ledger is required (requireMac or HETZER_AUDIT_REQUIRE_MAC=1). Anyone who can read the master key can forge a valid keyed ledger. Tail truncation is caught only by the head anchor file, which the same attacker can rewrite. Rotation is an operator action that anyone with shell access can also perform by moving files; it makes the recovery logged and carries the old head forward, but the new ledger does not enforce that the archive still exists, so deleting the archive together with the rotation entry is not detected. The SQLite audit table is a frozen mirror, not a second source of truth. Failures after the child process has started cannot undo it. The writer lock is not a queue: a waiter leaves a marker and writers pause briefly for a fresh one, which reduced rotation timeouts under 16 CPU-bound processes on Windows (5 of 25 rounds before, 1 of 25 after, small samples) but does not remove them or guarantee order, so a waiter (a rotation, a verification, another writer) can still time out after 10 seconds; fail-soft emitters then lose that event and --strict start events refuse to run. Measured on Windows only; Linux and macOS are untested.

results.name: SDK Contract and Vault Format Version (Gate G2)
results.target: sdk/index.mjs -> createHetzer(); cli/vault/hetzer-vault.mjs -> Grimoire format version check and format 2 migration, resolveMasterKey()
results.threat: The public SDK hands a credential value to its caller, accepts ids the vault and secretRef grammar do not, or runs a raw injection the vault did not grant; an older build changes a vault written by a newer format; the format 2 migration loses credentials, runs unrecorded, or leaves an upgraded installation with no key in silence
results.input: A synthetic vault with a credential whose value is also in its notes; credential ids with '.' and '_'; a raw-injection request against a credential whose grant denies it; vaults without a marker and with a newer marker, the latter with an old table layout; a format 1 vault with rows in the legacy tables and a damaged ledger; an environment that only sets the retired key alias
results.method: Walk the client and module member names; collect every SDK result and error for the value; run client.execution.run against the denied grant and check the child marker; open vaults and compare bytes, tables and columns before and after a refused open; open the format 1 vault while the ledger refuses, rotate the ledger and open again; resolve the master key with only the alias set
results.expected: No resolve, reveal, decrypt or lease member; only the SDK entry in the package exports; no value in any result or error; one id grammar; the denied child never starts and the error carries no value; new and unstamped vaults end at format 2 with credentials intact; a newer vault is refused with its bytes, tables and columns unchanged; a format 1 vault ends at format 2 with its credential intact, and its ledger record stays owed until the ledger takes it, then carries the dropped row counts and a MAC; the alias alone is refused with ERR_MASTER_KEY_ALIAS_RETIRED
results.observed: sdkHasNoRevealMember: true. packageExportsOnlySdk: true. sdkResultsHaveNoValue: true. idGrammarIsOne: true. sdkExecutionChecksGrant: true. freshVaultStamped: true. unstampedVaultRestamped: true. format1VaultMigrated: true. migrationRecordOwedUntilWritten: true. retiredKeyAliasRefused: true. newerVaultRefusedUntouched: true. inProcessCallerCanStillResolve: true.
results.boundary: The SDK narrows what a well-behaved caller can ask for. Code in the same process or under the same user can still import the vault module, call resolve() or read the database and key store (R-05 stays open for in-process callers; untrusted agents belong out of process in the sandbox). The package exports map limits specifiers, not file access. Lease interfaces are not part of apiVersion 1. Builds from before the format marker do not check it, so an older build can still open and alter a newer vault. The migration is one-way: rows in the dropped tables are counted in the audit record but not copied, and a build that checks the marker at format 1 refuses the migrated vault. The ledger record is written at least once (processes opening at the same moment can each write it) and only by a process that has the key. A legacy JSON vault is reported, not imported.

results.name: Master Key Kept Outside the Workspace
results.target: cli/core/cli.mjs -> initializeProject(); cli/vault/hetzer-vault.mjs -> locateMasterKey(), writeInstanceKey(), isolateMasterKey(); cli/vault/exec-policy.mjs -> SENSITIVE_HOST_PATTERNS
results.threat: A tool or model that can read the workspace (a coding agent, a compromised dependency, a sandbox that mounts the project) reads the master key next to the encrypted vault and decrypts every credential
results.input: A fresh workspace initialized with a temporary home directory; a workspace whose .env holds a key from an earlier build; a command string naming the key files
results.method: Initialize, scan every file under the workspace for the key bytes, check the key file mode, resolve the key, re-initialize, delete the key file and initialize again; isolate the legacy key and resolve it; classify the command strings
results.expected: The key is written only to ~/.hetzer/keys/<instance-id>.key with mode 0600 and no workspace file holds it; .env records only the non-secret instance id; re-initializing keeps the key; a missing key over an existing vault is refused with ERR_MASTER_KEY_NOT_FOUND instead of being replaced; isolate-key moves a legacy key out of .env; exec flags commands that name the key files
results.observed: keyFileOutsideWorkspace: true. keyFileOwnerOnly: true. noWorkspaceFileHoldsKey: true. envHasOnlyInstanceId: true. keyResolves: true. reinitKeepsKey: true. lostKeyRefused: true. isolateKeyMovesLegacyKey: true. execGuardNamesKeyFiles: true.
results.boundary: This removes the key from the workspace, not from the user account: any process running as the same OS user can still read ~/.hetzer/keys. It helps when the reader sees only the workspace (a sandbox that mounts the project, a repository upload, a backup of the project folder). A key supplied in HETZER_GRIMOIRE_KEY is never written to disk. Workspaces initialized before 0.7.0 keep their key in .env until 'hetzer creds isolate-key' moves it. The exec check matches command text, so a script that builds the path at run time is not caught; run untrusted code in the sandbox.

results.name: Container-Free srt Sandbox Settings and Engine Selection
results.target: cli/vault/srt-sandbox.mjs -> buildSrtSettings(), detectSrt(); cli/vault/sandbox.mjs -> selectSandboxEngine(), executeSandboxedProcess()
results.threat: Code running in the sandbox reads credentials under the home directory or the Hetzer files in the project, writes start-up files or Git hooks that run on the host later, or sends data to any host
results.input: A temporary home directory with ~/.ssh, a project inside it with .env and .git/hooks; requests to re-open ~/.ssh, write the home directory, allow every host, and use an allowlist with a container engine
results.method: Build the settings Hetzer passes to srt and inspect them; run the refusals; select engines with a fake probe; when srt is installed, run cat, touch and sh under srt with those settings and check the host file system afterwards
results.expected: Home and credential stores read-denied, project re-allowed with .env still hidden, writes only to the project and the run's own temporary directory, no network without a listed host; the unsafe requests refused; allowlist options select srt and are refused with a container engine; under a real srt the project is readable, the key and .env are not, and a hook or a file outside the project does not reach the host
results.observed: homeReadDenied: true. projectReadAllowed: true. workspaceEnvHidden: true. writesConfined: true. noNetworkByDefault: true. credentialStoreReopenRefused: true. homeWriteRefused: true. wildcardHostRefused: true. allowlistSelectsSrt: true. allowlistWithContainerRefused: true. enforcedByRealSrt: true. Enforcement: srt 0.0.78: projectReadable=true, sshKeyUnreadable=true, envHidden=true, hookNotWritable=true, outsideWriteKeptOff=true.
results.boundary: srt is an external program (Anthropic sandbox-runtime, tested with 0.0.78) using sandbox-exec on macOS and bubblewrap with seccomp on Linux; Hetzer generates its policy and does not reimplement it. Kernel and sandbox vulnerabilities are outside it. Every --sandbox-allow-read, --sandbox-allow-write and --sandbox-allow-host entry is reachable. Hetzer's extra project paths are denied only when they exist. Brokered credentials are refused under srt. The network allowlist is exercised by cli/vault/srt-sandbox.test.mjs where CI enables it, not by this protocol.

results.name: Agent Containment Defaults (hetzer agent)
results.threat: A coding agent runs on the host with the user's full access, or is started in a sandbox that still receives the workspace credentials or the master key
results.input: A workspace whose .env binds a raw-injectable credential, HETZER_GRIMOIRE_KEY in the environment, and a stand-in srt that records its arguments and environment
results.method: Run 'hetzer agent -- /bin/true' and inspect what the engine received and what the audit ledger recorded; run it again with --host
results.expected: The agent is started through srt with Hetzer's settings file; neither the credential nor the master key reaches it without --allow; SANDBOX_EXEC (agent: true) and AGENT_EXIT are recorded; --host is refused
results.observed: ranThroughSrt: true. noCredentialByDefault: true. masterKeyNotPassed: true. startAndExitRecorded: true. hostModeRefused: true.
results.boundary: The stand-in engine shows what Hetzer hands to srt, not srt's enforcement (VERIFY-SEC-017 covers that when srt is installed). The session uses the terminal directly, so its output is not redacted; a credential named with --allow and --allow-raw-unmediated is visible to the agent. The agent's own API key and state directory are outside Hetzer.

results.name: External Canary Decoys
results.threat: Code that reads files directly takes credentials without ever asking Hetzer, so a local tripwire never fires; or the decoy registry tells a reader which values are decoys; or the decoy is committed
results.input: A Git workspace with a .env; a two-variable decoy planted in .env.backup; an attempt to plant in the workspace .env
results.method: Plant, read the registry and the bait file, ask Git for the bait file's status, attempt the refused location, list and remove
results.expected: The decoy is in the bait file; the registry outside the workspace holds fingerprints, not values; Git does not see the bait file; the workspace .env is refused; list shows the decoy present; remove deletes both lines and the emptied file
results.observed: baitWritten: true. registryHoldsNoValue: true. registryOutsideWorkspace: true. keptOutOfGit: true. workspaceEnvRefused: true. listedPresent: true. removed: true.
results.boundary: The alert comes from the service that issued the decoy, when the decoy is used; Hetzer makes no network call and cannot confirm the alert works. A scraper that recognises the decoy or never uses what it collects sets off nothing. The bait file is readable inside the sandbox on purpose.
